## Methods facts

The run READMEs and harness metadata identify models `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-haiku-5-5`, effort medium, and Claude Code 2.1.278 with isolated configuration homes. ARBITER 1.0.0 ([public commit 2f549ae](https://github.com/AliSalman-et-al/ARBITER/commit/2f549ae30f056ff441ea61a04b719968716f2219)) was used for the runs. ARBITER-Sonnet ran on 12 October 2026 (12:12–19:17 EDT); the other arms ran on 14 October 2026, per their READMEs. Each arm ran each trial once. Run-to-run variability is not estimated. [AUTHORS: ARBITER 1.0.0 Zenodo DOI].

The ARBITER prompt invokes `/arbiter-assess`. The baseline uses the same minimal assessment request without the skill, followed by a fixed output-format instruction; the two prompts are not identical. Both templates and the verbatim baseline format instruction are quoted in the supplement. The ARBITER harness approved the proposed result unchanged and resumed with “Approved.” The protocol permitted uncoached “Continue.” replies at most twice per phase; observed counts are reported in the supplement. Baseline access was limited to Read, Glob and Grep, with no MCP server, skills or web tools; the supplied registry Markdown and acquired protocol/SAP documents preserved input parity.

The analysis includes 102 trials, after excluding atwine-2020, haney-2004 and herrmann-2016 for unsupported designs. Only the win share on consensus discordant cells is confirmatory. All other estimates are secondary or exploratory. Intervals use 10,000 percentile bootstrap replicates, resampling trials within each meta-analysis, seed `r SEED`. All estimates and paired contrasts use the same replicate weights. Blank CSV estimates and em dashes indicate undefined values. Metrics and differences are expressed on the 0–1 scale, except that agreement coefficients and differences can be negative. No p-values or multiplicity adjustment are used.

Missing arm judgements count as wrong. Ordinal coefficients for missing Haiku judgements use the documented maximal-disagreement penalty; an observed-cell sensitivity is supplied. The composite reference uses consensus preferred judgements on consensus disputed cells and meta labels on other cells, excluding split cells.

Adjudicators could only choose among the three labels offered. Cells where both Sonnet arms matched the meta label were never adjudicated and are assumed correct. Both features inflate absolute composite values for the Sonnet arms. Composite accuracy must not be presented as an accuracy claim in the abstract.

## Figure 1: architecture and draft trace

![ARBITER workflow and provisional worked trace from a committed assessment bundle. Source locators refer to captured PDF pages.](output/figures/figure1.png)

The trace uses a consensus cell where ARBITER-Sonnet matched the preferred judgement and differed from the meta label. Four more-severe candidates where only ARBITER departed from meta, plus levin-2016 D2, with cited bundle passages, evidence identifiers, source/page locators, verification status and abbreviated answer sets are in [worked-trace-candidates.csv](output/tables/worked-trace-candidates.csv). The default is award-10-2018 D2. The bundle records verification.json result = "verified", including content_hashes among its checks; it does not record a separate passage-level match status. The displayed selection is provisional for author review.

## Figure 2: study flow

![Benchmark inclusion and adjudication flow. Unsupported-design exclusions apply to every arm and analysis. The 62 differing consensus cells split into 54 ARBITER wins, 7 Baseline wins and 1 neither.](output/figures/figure2.png)

The analysis contains `r nrow(inputs$trials)` trials from `r n_distinct(inputs$trials$meta_id)` meta-analyses, `r nrow(cells)` disputed cells, `r sum(cells$consensus)` consensus cells and `r sum(!cells$consensus)` split cells.

On `r cons$n[1]` consensus discordant cells, ARBITER-Sonnet won `r cons$count[cons$metric=='ARBITER']`, baseline-Sonnet won `r cons$count[cons$metric=='Baseline']`, and neither won `r cons$count[cons$metric=='Neither']`. ARBITER win share was `r format_estimates(filter(cons,metric=='ARBITER'))` (95% CI).

## Table 2: agreement with meta labels

Cells are pooled D1–D5 (`r 102*5` per arm) or Overall (`r sum(!is.na(filter(inputs$labels,arm=='ARBITER-Sonnet',domain=='Overall')$meta))` per arm). Values are estimates (95% CI). Sensitivity and specificity classify Not Low using meta labels as the reference. All-Low reports accuracy and specificity only.

```{r}
show_metrics('table2')
show_metrics('table2-differences',c('comparison','domain'))
```

Pooled D1–D5 exact agreement with meta labels was `r headline('agreement-meta','accuracy','ARBITER-Sonnet','D1-D5')` for ARBITER-Sonnet and `r headline('agreement-meta','accuracy','Baseline-Sonnet','D1-D5')` for baseline-Sonnet. The latter reproduces 395/510.

## Table 3: algorithm consistency and audit

Domain algorithms use effect of assignment for D2. A required NA or missing answer makes a nonempty path invalid. Departure is Violation + Invalid answer path. Only absent labels or wholly absent answer sets are not evaluable, and excluded from rate denominators; their counts remain in the missing column. ARBITER domain consistency refers to the proposed judgement, with recorded overrides shown separately. Overall classifications distinguish exact consistency, permitted escalation, and violations.

```{r}
show_table(table_data('table3') |> filter(domain %in% c('D1-D5','Overall','Audit')) |>
  select(arm,domain,status,n,count,missing,estimate,lower,upper))
```

The proposed judgement agrees with the official domain algorithm in 510/510 ARBITER-Sonnet domains and 505/505 observed ARBITER-Haiku domains. The recorded override rates are 0/510 and 1/505 (0.2%), respectively. The hill-2017 D1 bundle records a Low to Some concerns override with rationale and evidence. Its adopted-label agreement with the algorithm is therefore 504/505 (99.8%). Five award-1-2014 domain labels remain missing. The amended gate passes. Judgements are algorithm-proposed; any model departure is recorded and auditable. Baseline violations are unrecorded departures.

Evidence coverage and structural bundle verification are the main grounding evidence. Baseline evidence traces are not available. Verification does not establish assessment correctness or completion. Required active answers were checked in every domain history record of the ARBITER bundles; both arms have zero invalid paths. Invalid-path sensitivity counts, resolving required NA/missing answers first as N/PN and then as NI, are in the supplement.

## Table 5: process metrics

```{r}
show_table(table_data('table5'))
```

Values are median [IQR], with paired mean ARBITER-Sonnet minus Baseline-Sonnet differences (95% CI), over 102 trials. Time is minutes per trial; input tokens are raw counts per trial (no decimals); cache creation and cache read tokens are millions per trial (two decimals); output and thinking tokens are thousands per trial (one decimal). Cost is a reconstructed API list-price equivalent in USD per trial under the frozen rate card in plan section 5.8; it is not expenditure. Thinking tokens are part of output tokens. Totals and Haiku results are in the supplement.

## Table 4: reliability of the reference standard

Disputed cells only (selected for disagreement with the meta label); not an estimate of overall meta-label accuracy. This restriction applies to all independent-judgement comparisons with source labels below.

```{r}
show_table(metric_table(table_data('table4-reliability'),c('comparison','population','n')))
show_table(table_data('meta-consensus-confusion') |>
  pivot_wider(names_from=preferred,values_from=n))
show_table(table_data('meta-leniency') |> select(direction,n,count,estimate,lower,upper))
```

```{r}
rel <- table_data('table4-reliability')
len <- table_data('meta-leniency')
```

Adjudicator A–Z weighted κ was `r estimate_ci(filter(rel,comparison=='A vs Z independent',metric=='kappa'))` on independent judgements and `r estimate_ci(filter(rel,comparison=='A vs Z preferred',metric=='kappa'))` on preferred judgements. Among consensus disputed cells, meta labels were less severe in `r len$count[len$direction=='Less severe']`/`r len$n[1]` cells (`r percent(len$estimate[len$direction=='Less severe'])`).

## Limitations facts and author completion

Adjudicators could only choose among the three offered labels. Unadjudicated cells where both Sonnet arms matched the meta label are assumed correct in the composite. These features inflate absolute composite values. Each arm assessed each trial once; run-to-run variability is not estimated. The final worked-trace selection, human taxonomy coding and checklist page/section references require author completion. Process times are harness measurements; costs are reconstructed API list-price equivalents; thinking tokens are reported separately and are part of output tokens. Trial PDFs are not redistributed; source DOIs and FILES.csv hashes identify them.
